passages.original: aut intra monasterium inflati quasi singulari scientia cunctos despicient. Oportet autem nos unam et simplicem apostolicam et patrum nostrorum imitari doctrinam, et gratia stabiliri, cor moresque subdere disciplinae, et ea cantare debemus quae, sicut beatus Augustinus dicit, ita scripta sunt, ut cantentur : quae autem non ita scripta sunt, non cantemus. Nec alio modo quam quo ipse Dominus jussit per prophetas et apostolos suos manifestari ea hominibus, debent a nobis in laude ipsius dici : ne quae cantanda sunt in modum prosae et quasi in lectionem mutemus, aut quae ita scripta sunt ut in ordine lectionum utamur, in tro- pis et cantilenae arte nostra praesumptione vertamus.
passages.english: or else, within the monastery, puffed up as though by some singular knowledge, they will look down on everyone. But we ought to imitate the one and simple teaching of the apostles and of our fathers, and to be made steadfast by grace, and to submit heart and conduct to discipline; and we ought to sing those things which, as blessed Augustine says, were written so as to be sung, but those which were not so written, let us not sing. Nor ought they to be spoken by us in his praise in any other way than that in which the Lord himself commanded them to be made known to men through his prophets and apostles: lest we change into the manner of prose, and as it were into a reading, the things that are to be sung, or, by our own presumption, turn into tropes and the art of chant the things that were written so that we might use them in the order of the readings.
passages.notes: "tro- pis" is a line-break split for "tropis" (tropes, i.e. liturgical musical/textual embellishments). "Cantilenae arte" rendered "the art of chant"; cantilena may carry a pejorative sense of elaborate or frivolous song.
